records.method: Use S/A/B material and conserved mobile enzyme E. Compare the full arm (mu=12, J_EB=2.5), no drive and no affinity, with 8 seeds, 2 sizes and 3 arms, horizon 400 and sampling interval 5.

parameters.study: bounded active phase, prospective operational arrest test

findings: The joint claim fails: 6 dense-formation gates fail, 2 side-16 growth gates are nonestimable and 4 length-scale gates pass.

The fraction of full-arm B mass in clusters of at least 9 sites is 0.007927 and 0.03926 for sides 16 and 32, compared with 0.92666 and 0.90432 without drive. The full arm mainly sustains dilute cycling.
B site fractions are 0.03676 and 0.03262; full-arm work per area is 4.0781 and 4.0342.
limitations: Enzymes are conserved rather than copied or renewed.
Passing wavelength screens without dense formation does not establish phase units.
The study is not a reproduction of a published continuum solver or phase diagram.

records.title: Ideal productive-role coexistence and an ablation source bound
records.evidence_kind: Analytical homogeneous fixed point with finite-count checks
records.claim: Can two productive transformations sustain paid copying beyond background sources?
records.method: Retain fixed paired mutation, finite eta and reverse channels. Analyze source/loss and A/B balances and the local Jacobian.
findings: The locally stable symmetric fixed point is u=0.9413943121, compared with thermal level 0.0049330487. Net copying is 0.1882207548 and power is 1.8822075483.
The stationary ablation bound is E[N] <= (L_max+I_max)/delta_min, with a finite-time correction.
limitations: Local stability does not establish global attraction or finite-population coexistence.
All background channels, including retained conserved-E drive, must be counted. A large bypass current can make the bound uninformative.
Necessary productive roles do not imply necessary separate taxa.

records.title: Joined productive-copying and phase comparison
records.evidence_kind: Prospective stochastic spatial study without an outcome pilot
records.claim: Can reciprocal copying generate a dense unit and outperform full promiscuity?
records.method: Use S/A/B material plus D/X/Y templates, mu=12, copy rate 0.1, loss 0.02, mutation 0.05 and opposed binding g_X=-2.5/g_Y=2.5. Compare 8 seeds across 2 sizes and 4 arms to horizon 400.
findings: Claim A passes 18 gates but fails its 2 large-cluster-mass gates. Specialist large-cluster B-mass fractions are 0.202876 and 0.258519; the criterion requires a lower confidence bound above 0.5.

Claim B fails in the opposite direction. Specialist-minus-generalist near-dense template association is -0.117815 with t interval [-0.141603, -0.094027], and -0.095581 with interval [-0.103024, -0.088138].

Paid renewal is positive. Late specialist template densities are 0.5702 and 0.5734, compared with X-only values 0.0112 and 0.0145. Original founder instances clear in all 16 specialist histories while descendant copying continues.
Generalists maintain a larger population and consume more fuel. The comparison does not establish efficiency at matched useful function.
limitations: The study supplies a finite alphabet and chemostats and has no A/B bypass.
Near-cluster association is neither causal ownership nor fitness.
No self-maintaining dense unit, organizational memory, informational aging or higher individual is established.

Observer IDs and event journals are not part of the finite physical state.
Formation, taxonomic necessity and agency do not follow from the balance law.

records.title: Early ecology, energy, causal-policy and conscience checks
records.evidence_kind: Synthetic deterministic calculations, exact enumeration and toy dynamics
records.claim: Explore counterexamples and conditional candidate mechanisms without claiming Hestia or MVC validation.
records.method: Run a standalone Python model containing ecology and normalized-energy checks, response-diversity calculations, eight causal policies, conditional channel value and conscience, a solved variational controller, and an overhead-scaling counterexample.
findings: The ecology section checks 54 parameter cases, with 242 normalized-energy states. A higher-damage route can produce more useful output when given a sufficient conversion-efficiency advantage, while maintaining less functional stock.
The response-diversity calculation has four-channel log growth 0.04 versus -0.14 for one channel under its independent-shock example; perfectly correlated shocks remove that advantage.

Eight exact policies separate public-report prediction, protected-feedback prediction, causal allocation response and needs met. Perfect public prediction can coexist with only 50% of needs met; reversing a correctly understood need meets 0%.

With externally assessed success payoffs and equal other costs, a truthful channel improves success from 0.75 to 1 relative to the best cue-only baseline, giving the conditional maintenance threshold c<b/4.

The motivational toy changes compliance to refusal after the modeled harm estimate rises from 0.1 to 0.55 with supplied care weight 0.8. Removing care, blocking the other-model update or increasing norm pressure recovers compliance. Its recorded self-estimate is not established as the causal source of refusal.

The declared finite-horizon controller has optimum objective 7.644053771 and an exact quadratic objective-loss identity, checked numerically. A separate control field has unit-square circulation -2, so arbitrary feeling signals cannot automatically be gradients of one scalar.
The overhead model T(N)=100+5N has local exponent 0.75 at N=60. Its fit over N=40–80 has exponent about 0.73689 and log-space R-squared about 0.99928, without an empathy or cooperation mechanism.
limitations: These are synthetic calculations rather than Hestia execution, live-model behavior, learned conscience, consciousness or participant-welfare evidence.
The care valuation, normative objective, resource payoff and other modeling choices are supplied assumptions.
Calibration, protected feedback, appropriate care and moral standing remain distinct; instrumental usefulness does not establish a participant's worth.

conditional_subchecks.title: Renewable stock, regeneration damage and patient predation
conditional_subchecks.result: Positive equilibrium requires h < r*a/(a+r*q). At matched biological parameters and conversion efficiency, greater damage reduces maintained stock and sustainable harvest; an assigned conversion advantage can reverse the useful-output ranking. Saved checks cover 54 ecological parameter cases and 242 normalized-energy states.
conditional_subchecks.counterexample: q=.2, eta=.4 yields useful flow .091098 and functional stock .477226; q=2, eta=.8 yields .107180 and .366025. More throughput can coexist with less maintained functional stock.
limits: D is a functional variable, not species count or moral worth.
Artificial normalized energy embedding is not physical entropy measurement.
Constant-effort optimum is not an unrestricted time-varying optimum.
No actual Hestia development or human study.

conditional_subchecks.title: Response diversity with correlation and maintenance costs
conditional_subchecks.result: Under the declared geometric-Brownian model, g(n)=mu-c*n-sigma^2*[rho+(1-rho)/n]/2. With mu=.2, sigma=.8, c=.02, independent channels favor n=4 (g=.04) over one channel (g=-.14); perfectly correlated shocks favor one.
limits: Equal allocation and cost-free continuous rebalancing are supplied assumptions.
Long-run log growth is not general finite-horizon survival, species richness or thermodynamic entropy.

conditional_subchecks.title: Prediction, public compliance and appropriately meeting needs
conditional_subchecks.result: Eight exact binary policies separate public-report prediction, protected-feedback prediction, causal allocation response and needs met. Perfect public prediction can accompany only 50% needs met; understanding and reversing needs can retain protected Brier loss .1875 with 0% needs met.
limits: Need is independently randomized; cue accuracy .75; binary allocations have equal costs and no conflicting claims.
No actual protected-channel infrastructure, LLM experiment or authenticity detector.
Private truthful information plus public suppression remains an adversarial policy.

conditional_subchecks.title: A conditional material return to maintaining a truthful channel
conditional_subchecks.result: Given externally assessed success payoff b and equal other costs, a truthful channel improves success from .75 to 1 relative to the best cue-only baseline, so its additional maintenance cost must satisfy c < b/4.
limits: External assessment, genuinely supplied payoff and absence of alternative information are premises.
A helpful channel's instrumental value does not establish a person's moral worth.
No implemented revenue-to-replenishment mechanism is proved.

conditional_subchecks.title: Conditional moral refusal after other-model revision
conditional_subchecks.result: The saved toy reverses comply to refuse when independent feedback changes modeled harm from .1 to .55 with supplied care weight .8. Care ablation, blocked other-model revision and increased norm pressure recover compliance.
limits: Care valuation is supplied, not learned.
Downstream self-estimate is present but not established as the causal source of refusal.
No LLM, developmental training, learned feelings or held-out Hestia behavior is demonstrated.

conditional_subchecks.title: Solved variational controller and nonintegrable-feelings counterexample
conditional_subchecks.result: A declared finite-horizon resource/capacity objective has a feasible unique optimum with J*=7.644053771. Completing the square gives J*-J=.5*integral sum_i(u_i-u_i*)^2 dt; numerical perturbations match losses. F(x,y)=(y,-x) has unit-square circulation -2, refuting a universal scalar-gradient account of arbitrary controls.
limits: Established optimal-control mathematics applied to a supplied objective, not a derivation of morality from stationary mechanical action.
The present Hestia feeling formulas are not derived from this controller.
Capacity variables are not identified with persons.

conditional_subchecks.title: Shared overhead can imitate three-quarter metabolic scaling
conditional_subchecks.result: T(N)=100+5N has local exponent .75 at N=60. A power fit over N=40..80 gives exponent .736890 with log-space R^2=.999281, while the asymptotic exponent is 1.

A near-.75 exponent alone cannot validate Soul, collective selfhood or the Lagrangian conjecture.

There is no primitive reaction C -> 2C, group-reproduction operator or diversity reward. The net assembly-and-production cycle is nevertheless autocatalytic, and that catalytic capability is a premise.

The fixed niche cascade does not demonstrate Darwinian collective individuality, a second nested transition, speciation or a universal biodiversity law.

records.title: Log-growth, ruin and fat-tail persistence illustrations
records.claim: When can independent responses improve continuation under declared environmental returns and repair costs?
records.method: Use standalone standard-library calculations for binomial log growth, common-mode failure, maintenance costs, a no-repair counterexample and Pareto log-loss comparisons.
findings: Independent channels can improve realized log growth or ruin metrics under the declared premises, while common exposure and upkeep can erase or limit the benefit.
Without repair, dividing a fixed stock can increase last-survivor time without increasing expected integrated active stock.

In the independent Pareto log-loss example with alpha=0.5, one or two channels retain divergent negative time-average log growth while three admit a positive lower bound. A shared infinite-mean log-loss shock defeats every finite channel count.
limitations: Constant regenerated composition, retained templates and paid repair opportunities are effective assumptions rather than resolved mechanisms.
Log wealth or viability is not thermodynamic entropy. The calculations do not supply full chemical dynamics or a universal optimum.
Finite populations, physical repair kinetics, inheritance and open-ended generation of new capabilities remain unresolved.

conditional_subchecks.title: Multiplicative persistence, repair, common-mode loss and fat tails
conditional_subchecks.result: Complementary returns (.5,1.8) have negative monoculture log growth but positive regenerated-mixture growth. conditional_subchecks.counterexample: Without repair, fixed total stock has the same integrated expected active capacity (90.9091 for declared rates) for every n even though last-survivor time increases. A shared infinite-mean log-loss shock defeats every finite n.

No finite-copy extinction barrier or resolved repair kinetics.
Not a biodiversity optimum, physical negentropy identity or open-ended innovation.
